title: Prefill priority playbook - personal lab notes
content:
Goal:
Reduce p99 tail for mixed-priority workloads by pre-populating KV cache and adding a lightweight prefill prioritization lane. Quick lab scratchpad to capture what I tried, numbers, and next steps.

Background/context:
- We often see p99 spikes when a low-priority batch evicts key blocks used by imminent high-priority requests.
- Hypothesis: explicit small prefill requests (cheap prefix steps) for hot keys + a fast priority queue for prefill + preferential eviction heuristics will (a) reduce cold-cache cost for high-priority traffic and (b) keep throughput intact.
- This doc captures an iterative micro-benchmark run on a small cluster to validate the idea and tune parameters.

Test harness & environment:
- Model: redwood-13b-q4 (quantized) -- same model binary used across runs.
- Hardware: 1x A100-40GB (single GPU), driver stack: CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS/cuDNN matched to production image.
- Runtime: local runtime build (commit a7d3c9) with prefill-lane experiment toggles.
- Client harness: bench-runner v0.9.2 (parallel connections, synthetic arrival generator).
- Workload: mixed-priority Poisson arrivals across two priority classes: high (10% of requests) and low (90%). High requests have short contexts (avg 60 tokens), low requests are longer (avg 300 tokens).
- Concurrency target: target steady qps 120 (aggregate).

Key knobs tested:
1) prefill_fraction: fraction of incoming requests that trigger an explicit prefill on the backend (0.0 - 0.5)
2) prefill_batch_size: how many tokens to prefill per prefill request (8, 16, 32)
3) prefill_priority_window: whether prefill requests run on a fast preemptive lane (true/false)
4) eviction_bias: prefer evicting cold long-context KV vs short-context hot KV (0.0 - 1.0)

Commands (representative):
- baseline (no prefill): ./bench-runner --model redwood-13b-q4 --qps 120 --prio-mix 10,90 --concurrency 32 --duration 900 --tag baseline
- prefill run: ./bench-runner --model redwood-13b-q4 --qps 120 --prio-mix 10,90 --concurrency 32 --duration 900 --prefill 0.15 --prefill-size 16 --prefill-priority true --evict-bias 0.7 --tag prefill-0.15

Raw run notes (short log):
- 2024-09-12 10:14 - baseline start (warmup 120s)
  - p50: 38ms, p95: 180ms, p99: 420ms, throughput: 119.6 qps (target 120)
  - observations: periodic p99 spikes every ~60s correlated with long low-priority calls finishing and triggering large KV churn.

- 2024-09-12 14:30 - prefill-0.15 (prefill_fraction=0.15, prefill_size=16, prefill_priority=true, evict_bias=0.7)
  - p50: 42ms, p95: 140ms, p99: 210ms, throughput: 118.9 qps
  - first ~2 minutes: slight increase in p50 (CPU on client side due to more small prefill RPCs) but p99 collapsed ~2x vs baseline.
  - memory/KV hit-rate: overall KV hit-rate for hot keys moved from ~67% -> ~91% for high-priority requests.
  - CPU/GPU utilization: +3% GPU, +6% CPU. No out-of-memory events.

Sweep summary (selected runs):
- baseline: p50=38ms p95=180ms p99=420ms qps=119.6
- prefill 0.05 size 8 priority true evict 0.6: p50=40ms p95=165ms p99=330ms qps=119.2
- prefill 0.10 size 16 priority true evict 0.7: p50=41ms p95=150ms p99=260ms qps=119.0
- prefill 0.15 size 16 priority true evict 0.7: p50=42ms p95=140ms p99=210ms qps=118.9
- prefill 0.25 size 32 priority true evict 0.8: p50=46ms p95=175ms p99=240ms qps=117.5 (too many prefill ops hurt p50 due to client-side RPC overhead)
- prefill 0.15 size 16 priority false evict 0.7: p50=40ms p95=160ms p99=340ms qps=119.1 (priority lane materially helps p99)

Interpretation / quick conclusions:
- Small fraction prefill (~10-15%) with small prefill size (8-16 tokens) and a fast preemptive lane yields the best p99 reduction with minimal throughput impact.
- Prefill overhead shows up mostly on p50 (slight increase) and small CPU raise; acceptable tradeoff for services that prioritize p99 for high-priority requests.
- Prefill-only without priority lane yields significantly smaller improvements; latency isolation provided by the prefill-priority lane is critical.
- Diminishing returns past prefill_fraction ~0.15; higher fractions increase client RPC overhead and start to erode p50/p95.
- Eviction bias towards evicting long-context low-priority KV (evict_bias >= 0.7) complements prefill strategy.

Quick heuristics for prod config (starter):
- prefill_fraction: 0.12
- prefill_size: 16 tokens
- prefill_priority_lane: enabled (short, preemptive lane with capped concurrent prefill slots per GPU: 4)
- eviction_bias: 0.7 (prefer evicting large low-priority KV blocks)
- client-side batching: coalesce prefill RPCs per-client up to 8 prefill ops to reduce RPC pressure

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How does the strategy behave under multi-GPU, distributed KV partitioning? Need to test cross-GPU cache warm-up dynamics (next: 2 x A100 cluster test).
- Evaluate effect on cost: extra token work from prefill (15% * 16 tokens) ~ +2.4 tokens/request on average; run cost model.
- Interactions with quantized kernels: do prefill ops stress a different kernel path that could affect thermal or scheduler fairness?
- Is there a simple RL or heuristic to choose per-customer prefill_fraction based on observed hot-key churn?

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] Re-run with 2xGPU partitioned KV and measure inter-GPU warmup time (target: 2024-09-20).
- [ ] Add end-to-end client batching for prefill to bench-runner (reduce p50 hit).
- [ ] Share numbers with Maya, tag PR with bench results, open RFC for prefill priority lane design doc.
- [ ] Check Linear ISSUE-2041 for integration with rollout/flag gates.

Small ASCII trend sketch (p99 vs prefill_fraction at size=16, priority lane on):
- prefill 0.00 -> 420ms
- prefill 0.05 -> 330ms
- prefill 0.10 -> 260ms
- prefill 0.15 -> 210ms
- prefill 0.20 -> 230ms

Final note (handwave):
Prefill is promising as a low-risk, incremental mitigation for tail latency when combined with a tiny scheduling primitive. Worth prototyping at 2-node scale and measuring cross-tenant effects before broader rollout.

---
Appendix: short config snippet used in runtime (for copy/paste)
runtime.cfg:
  prefill_enabled: true
  prefill_fraction: 0.15  # tuned in lab
  prefill_size_tokens: 16
  prefill_priority_lane: true
  prefill_max_parallel_per_gpu: 4
  eviction_bias: 0.7

Bench command example:
./bench-runner --model redwood-13b-q4 --qps 120 --prio-mix 10,90 --prefill 0.15 --prefill-size 16 --prefill-priority true --duration 900 --out results/prefill-0.15.json

End of scratchpad.
